prerequisites.reason: The compactness argument uses sets, indexed collections, functions, inverse images, and constructions with arbitrary sequences; the proof patterns also require the earlier quantified reasoning.

The interval-compactness and subsequence proofs invoke the least-upper-bound property and nested closed intervals. These completeness facts are used here rather than developed from the real-number foundations.

background: Elementary inequalities, absolute values, factoring a difference of squares, and the triangle inequality. Epsilon-N and epsilon-delta definitions are introduced in this lecture.
readiness_checks: In “for every positive epsilon there exists N such that every n at least N works,” which choices may depend on earlier choices, and what would its negation say?
Can you explain the difference between an inverse image of a set and an inverse function, and verify that inverse images preserve intersections?
Can you explain why a bounded nondecreasing real sequence converges by using the supremum of its values?
